subtopics.title: Plot the basic sine graph
subtopics.exposition: Rounded to 2 decimal places, sin θ for θ = 0°, 30°, 60°, 90°, 120°, 150°, 180°, 210°, 240°, 270°, 300°, 330°, 360° is 0; 0.5; 0.87; 1; 0.87; 0.5; 0; -0.5; -0.87; -1; -0.87; -0.5; 0 respectively. The graph of y = sin θ has a wave shape. To plot y = sin θ for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, use a calculator to complete a table of values of sin θ for θ = 0°, 30°, 60°, 90°, 120°, 150°, 180°, 210°, 240°, 270°, 300°, 330° and 360°. After completing the table, plot the points and join them with a smooth curve to get the graph of y = sin θ. When plotting y = sin θ, choose an appropriate scale and plot the values of θ on the x-axis and the values of sin θ on the y-axis. The calculated values of sin θ in the table are rounded to 2 decimal places.

subtopics.title: Sketch y = a sin θ + q
subtopics.exposition: In the equation y = a sin θ + q, a and q are constants and they have different effects on the graph. The effect of q is called a vertical shift, because the whole sine graph shifts up or down by q units. The value of a affects the amplitude of the graph, which is the height of the peaks and the depth of the troughs. For q > 0, the graph is shifted vertically upwards by q units. For q < 0, the graph is shifted vertically downwards by q units. For q = 0, the graph is the basic sine graph. For a > 1, there is a vertical stretch and the amplitude increases. For 0 < a < 1, there is a vertical contraction and the amplitude decreases. For a = 1, the graph is the basic sine graph. For a < 0, there is a reflection about the x-axis. For -1 < a < 0, there is a reflection about the x-axis and the amplitude decreases. For a < -1, there is a reflection about the x-axis and the amplitude increases. The graph for -1 < a < 0 is the reflection about the x-axis of the graph for 0 < a < 1. The graph for a < -1 is the reflection about the x-axis of the graph for a > 1. To investigate the effect of q, plot y = sin θ - 2, y = sin θ - 1, y = sin θ, y = sin θ + 1 and y = sin θ + 2 on the same set of axes for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, then use the results to deduce the effect of q. To investigate the effect of a, plot y = -2 sin θ, y = -sin θ, y = sin θ and y = 2 sin θ on the same set of axes for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, then use the results to deduce the effect of a. To sketch f(θ) = 2 sin θ + 3, first examine the standard form of the equation: a > 1, so the graph is stretched vertically, and q > 0, so the graph is shifted vertically upwards by 3 units. Next, substitute values of θ from 0° to 360° in steps of 30° into f(θ) to complete a table of values. For f(θ) = 2 sin θ + 3, the values of f(θ) at θ = 0°, 30°, 60°, 90°, 120°, 150°, 180°, 210°, 240°, 270°, 300°, 330°, 360° are 3; 4; 4.73; 5; 4.73; 4; 3; 2; 1.27; 1; 1.27; 2; 3 respectively. Finally, plot the points and join them with a smooth curve to sketch the graph.

subtopics.title: Characteristics of sine graph
subtopics.exposition: Each complete wave of the sine graph takes 360° to complete; this is called the period. The height of the wave above and below the x-axis is called the graph's amplitude. A period of 360° means that one sine wave is completed in 360°. The maximum value of y = sin θ is 1 and the minimum value is -1. For y = sin θ the domain is [0°, 360°] and the range is [-1, 1]. The x-intercepts of y = sin θ are (0°, 0), (180°, 0) and (360°, 0), and the y-intercept is (0°, 0). The maximum turning point of y = sin θ is (90°, 1) and the minimum turning point is (270°, -1). For f(θ) = a sin θ + q, the domain is [0°, 360°]. The range of f(θ) = a sin θ + q depends on the values of a and q. For a > 0 and for all values of θ, f(θ) = a sin θ + q is always between -a+q and a+q. For a > 0, the range of f(θ) = a sin θ + q is [-a+q, a+q]. For a < 0, the range of f(θ) = a sin θ + q is [a+q, -a+q]. The period of y = a sin θ + q is 360°. The y-intercept of f(θ) = a sin θ + q is the point (0, q). To find the range for a > 0, start from -1 ≤ sin θ ≤ 1, obtain -a ≤ a sin θ ≤ a, then add q to each part to get -a+q ≤ a sin θ + q ≤ a+q, that is -a+q ≤ f(θ) ≤ a+q. The y-intercept of f(θ) = a sin θ + q is found as the value of f(θ) at θ = 0°. Substituting θ = 0° gives y = f(0°) = a sin 0° + q = a(0) + q = q. For f(θ) = 2 sin θ + 3, the range is [1, 5], there are no x-intercepts, and the y-intercept is (0°, 3). For f(θ) = 2 sin θ + 3, the maximum turning point is (90°, 5) and the minimum turning point is (270°, 1).

subtopics.title: Find a and q from graph
subtopics.exposition: The y-intercept of the graph of y = a sin θ + q is the point (0, q), so the value of q is the y-value at θ = 0°.

claims.claim: To plot y = sin θ for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, use a calculator to complete a table of values of sin θ for θ = 0°, 30°, 60°, 90°, 120°, 150°, 180°, 210°, 240°, 270°, 300°, 330° and 360°.
When plotting y = sin θ, choose an appropriate scale and plot the values of θ on the x-axis and the values of sin θ on the y-axis.
The calculated values of sin θ in the table are rounded to 2 decimal places.
After completing the table, plot the points and join them with a smooth curve to get the graph of y = sin θ.
The graph of y = sin θ has a wave shape.
Each complete wave of the sine graph takes 360° to complete; this is called the period.
The height of the wave above and below the x-axis is called the graph's amplitude.
The maximum value of y = sin θ is 1 and the minimum value is -1.
For y = sin θ the domain is [0°, 360°] and the range is [-1, 1].
The x-intercepts of y = sin θ are (0°, 0), (180°, 0) and (360°, 0), and the y-intercept is (0°, 0).
The maximum turning point of y = sin θ is (90°, 1) and the minimum turning point is (270°, -1).
In the equation y = a sin θ + q, a and q are constants and they have different effects on the graph.

To investigate the effect of q, plot y = sin θ - 2, y = sin θ - 1, y = sin θ, y = sin θ + 1 and y = sin θ + 2 on the same set of axes for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, then use the results to deduce the effect of q.
To investigate the effect of a, plot y = -2 sin θ, y = -sin θ, y = sin θ and y = 2 sin θ on the same set of axes for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, then use the results to deduce the effect of a.
The effect of q is called a vertical shift, because the whole sine graph shifts up or down by q units.
For q > 0, the graph is shifted vertically upwards by q units.
For q < 0, the graph is shifted vertically downwards by q units.
For q = 0, the graph is the basic sine graph.
The value of a affects the amplitude of the graph, which is the height of the peaks and the depth of the troughs.
For a > 1, there is a vertical stretch and the amplitude increases.
For 0 < a < 1, there is a vertical contraction and the amplitude decreases.
For a = 1, the graph is the basic sine graph.
For a < 0, there is a reflection about the x-axis.
For -1 < a < 0, there is a reflection about the x-axis and the amplitude decreases.
For a < -1, there is a reflection about the x-axis and the amplitude increases.
The graph for -1 < a < 0 is the reflection about the x-axis of the graph for 0 < a < 1.
The graph for a < -1 is the reflection about the x-axis of the graph for a > 1.
Amplitude is always positive.
When sketching trigonometric graphs, always start with the basic graph and then consider the effects of a and q.
To sketch f(θ) = 2 sin θ + 3, first examine the standard form of the equation: a > 1, so the graph is stretched vertically, and q > 0, so the graph is shifted vertically upwards by 3 units.
Next, substitute values of θ from 0° to 360° in steps of 30° into f(θ) to complete a table of values.
Finally, plot the points and join them with a smooth curve to sketch the graph.
For f(θ) = a sin θ + q, the domain is [0°, 360°].
The range of f(θ) = a sin θ + q depends on the values of a and q.
To find the range for a > 0, start from -1 ≤ sin θ ≤ 1, obtain -a ≤ a sin θ ≤ a, then add q to each part to get -a+q ≤ a sin θ + q ≤ a+q, that is -a+q ≤ f(θ) ≤ a+q.
For a > 0 and for all values of θ, f(θ) = a sin θ + q is always between -a+q and a+q.
For a > 0, the range of f(θ) = a sin θ + q is [-a+q, a+q].
For a < 0, the range of f(θ) = a sin θ + q is [a+q, -a+q].
The period of y = a sin θ + q is 360°.
A period of 360° means that one sine wave is completed in 360°.
The y-intercept of f(θ) = a sin θ + q is found as the value of f(θ) at θ = 0°.
Substituting θ = 0° gives y = f(0°) = a sin 0° + q = a(0) + q = q.
The y-intercept of f(θ) = a sin θ + q is the point (0, q).
For f(θ) = 2 sin θ + 3, the range is [1, 5], there are no x-intercepts, and the y-intercept is (0°, 3).
For f(θ) = 2 sin θ + 3, the maximum turning point is (90°, 5) and the minimum turning point is (270°, 1).
The y-intercept of the graph of y = a sin θ + q is the point (0, q), so the value of q is the y-value at θ = 0°.
